Malaysia’s Pacific Meridian Bank placed in administration amid mounting losses

KUALA LUMPUR, June 18 – Malaysia’s Pacific Meridian Bank Berhad was placed into administration on Tuesday following mounting financial losses, in what industry analysts say is one of the country’s largest banking insolvencies in over a decade.

The Central Bank of Malaysia confirmed the move, citing “persistent capital inadequacy and an inability to meet regulatory requirements.” The bank’s branches nationwide were closed to customers early Tuesday, with online banking services also suspended. ATMs operated by Pacific Meridian Bank have been disabled, according to notices posted at affected locations.

“Pacific Meridian Bank’s position had become unsustainable despite efforts to recapitalise and restructure. The appointment of administrators is aimed at protecting depositors and preserving the orderly functioning of the financial system,” the central bank said in a statement.

The bank, which held assets valued at over 18 billion ringgit ($3.8 billion) and served more than 600,000 retail and corporate customers, had struggled with rising loan defaults and falling profitability over the past year. Industry sources said talks with potential investors had collapsed last week, prompting regulators to intervene.

Customers were seen gathering outside several branches in Kuala Lumpur and Penang seeking information. “We are working closely with the administrators to address customer concerns and will provide updates as the process continues,” said Nurul Azizah, a spokesperson for Pacific Meridian Bank.

The Malaysian Banking Association said in a statement that the sector remains “well-capitalised and resilient,” describing Pacific Meridian Bank’s situation as “isolated.” Financial analysts expect the administration process to focus on assessing the bank’s loan book and options for restructuring or sale of assets.

No timeline has been given for the completion of the administration process, with further updates expected from regulators in coming days.
